meta: A lone figure in a river and mountain landscape by Xiang Shengmo, a Ming scholar-painter who sold his work after the dynasty fell.
about: Xiang Shengmo was a grandson of the noted connoisseur and collector Xiang Yuanbian, who lived from 1525 to 1590. He drew on many ancient sources for small landscapes the museum describes as carefully drawn and quiet in mood. The lone figure here probably stands for a scholar-official who has left society for the solitude of nature, an ideal Xiang and other artists held. When the Ming dynasty collapsed and his family lost its wealth, he had to sell his paintings to live.

meta: Mr. Veacock, Thomas Birch's brother-in-law, in the officer's uniform he wore in the War of 1812.
about: Mr. Veacock was Thomas Birch's brother-in-law. He is shown in an officer's uniform, and he fought in the War of 1812. The high collar of his jacket reflects the rule by 1812 that it should reach the tip of the ear and, in front, as high as the chin would allow when turning the head. Birch painted him around 1800.

meta: Elizabeth Nourse painted a cold fisher girl on the Étaples dunes in 1889, while the model reportedly wept from the wind.
about: In the summer of 1889 Elizabeth Nourse traveled around northern France with her sister Louise and their Cincinnati friend Anna Schmidt. It was a bitterly cold day when she painted this scene, and Anna later wrote that the model wept from the cold and wind on the Étaples dunes. The model's pink cheeks and limbs suggest how uncomfortable the blustery air was that day.

meta: A design for a boat-shaped vessel held up by two nudes, with harpies and a ram's head, by Luzio Romano, about 1540.
about: This is a design for a boat-shaped vessel on a baluster pedestal, with two nudes sitting on either side and raising their arms as if holding it up. A long-necked winged harpy curves beneath the spout or prow, and a harpy or female half-figure at the stern curves outward, her tail forming the handle. A figure frieze runs along the body, with a ram's head at the center. Luzio Romano made the design around 1540.

meta: Two elephants fight before the Mughal emperor Muhammad Shah in Nainsukh's painting of about 1730 to 1740, a second version in Cleveland.
about: Muhammad Shah, who ruled from 1719 to 1748, enjoyed watching elephants fight. He is shown at his window of public audience, marked by a golden carpet, smoking a hookah, while women of his harem watch from behind painted screens. Pairs of men with fire brands and spears keep the elephants in check. Nainsukh came from a small kingdom in the western Himalayas and painted scenes of his experiences at the Mughal court in Delhi.

meta: A young woman plucks a partridge in a kitchen with a child and a small dog in Willem Joseph Laquy's The Kitchen, about 1760.
about: In the middle of a kitchen a young woman sits by a basket plucking a partridge. A kitchen maid comes in from the right with a tray of fish, and at the left a child sits in a chair playing with a small dog. A copper kettle with vegetables and a broken jug stand at the front right, and a painting hangs over the hearth at the back. A game crown with a partridge hangs from the ceiling. Willem Joseph Laquy painted it.

meta: The headless ghost of Lord Lovat walks a graveyard at night in Samuel Ireland's satirical print Lovat's Ghost on Pilgrimage, about 1790.
about: The headless ghost of Simon Fraser, 11th Lord Lovat, walks through a cemetery at night in a monk's robes, holding his head in his left hand and a walking stick in his right. Under the picture is the title, followed by a satirical poem. Samuel Ireland made the print around 1790.

meta: A woman holds a wreath over a bust of Jacques Necker under the sun of Louis XVI, a panel design by Claude-Louis Desrais, about 1780.
about: A radiant sun with interlaced L's, the symbol of Louis XVI, shines at the top, with a woman deflecting its beams with a magnifying glass. At the center a woman holds a wreath over a portrait bust of Jacques Necker. A book titled Compte rendu stands at the foot of the plinth, with a scroll reading Eloge de Colbert. At the bottom are a grotesque and a crowned shield with fleurs-de-lis. Claude-Louis Desrais made the design.

meta: Maria Henrietta Stuart, widow of William II, visits Bartholomeus van der Helst's studio in Hendrik Jacobus Scholten's painting of 1850.
about: The Princess of Orange, Mary Henrietta Stuart, the widow of Prince William II, visits the studio of Bartholomeus van der Helst. In the background hangs his Banquet of the Civic Guard of 1648. She holds a fan, and two gentlemen and a woman accompany her. Hendrik Jacobus Scholten painted the scene, which the catalog dates to 1850.

meta: A sugar plantation on the Suriname River, painted by Dirk Valkenburg in 1707 for its owner Jonas Witsen, who sent him there to map his property.
about: This shows one of the many sugar plantations along the Suriname River. The Rijksmuseum notes that the plantation itself and the many people enslaved there are missing. Jonas Witsen, an Amsterdam slaveholder who inherited three plantations from his wife in 1702, sent Dirk Valkenburg to Suriname to record his property. In the foreground are a few Lokono, one of the area's original peoples, with a house of palm leaves, and a brick house stands behind the awara palms.

meta: Robert Broome in a miniature worn as a stickpin, painted by Anson Dickinson about 1810.
about: Robert Broome was the uncle of Robert Munroe, who was the great-uncle of the donor, Helen Munroe, once director of publications at the Smithsonian. This miniature was worn as a stickpin, one of the flashiest accessories a gentleman could have then, and its unusual close-up profile of the sitter would have drawn attention. Anson Dickinson painted it.

meta: A trophy of a lyre, bow, torch and winged beast between a fire tripod and a candle stand, a design by Carlo Bianconi, about 1770.
about: A trophy made of a lyre, a bow, arrows, a quiver, a torch, an olive branch, a ribbon, an urn and a fantastic winged beast stands between a tripod holding fire on the left and a burning candle stand on the right. The back has a sketch of the ground plan of a building. Carlo Bianconi made the design around 1770.

meta: Queen Esther by the English painter Edwin Long, painted in 1878 and held in Melbourne.
about: Queen Esther is an oil on canvas painting by the English artist Edwin Long, made in 1878. It is held at the National Gallery of Victoria in Melbourne. Wikipedia gives no more than that about the picture.
